question: Can a susceptibility matrix that linearly maps infinitesimal training-distribution changes to posterior structural observables be pseudo-inverted to design finite data reweightings that reproducibly control which circuit forms or which equally training-compatible algorithm a neural network learns?

key_findings.claim: The paper formulates patterning as a local inverse problem: the minimum-Euclidean-norm linearized data intervention for a target structural change is dh = chi-dagger dmu, with singular modes pairing principal data patterns to principal structures.
key_findings.evidence: Starting from derivatives of annealed-posterior expectation values with respect to data-mixture coordinates, the paper defines per-token susceptibilities as posterior covariances, stacks them into chi, and applies the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse. Its SVD derivation shows that a target aligned with left singular vector u_beta is produced by reweighting along v_beta/sigma_beta; targets in chi's left null space are inaccessible to the chosen data perturbations.

anchors.section: 2.3 Mode decomposition and the patterning solution; Equations 18-21

key_findings.claim: Reweighting tokens along the induction-associated PC2 direction changes when and how strongly induction structure develops in the studied 3M-parameter language model.
key_findings.evidence: Four models were trained for each of Repress-0x, Baseline-1x, Induce-2x, and Induce-4x. Repress-0x reduces induction-pattern susceptibilities by roughly an order of magnitude and leaves prefix-matching scores near the floor through 20,000 steps; 2x and 4x weighting move the susceptibility rise and induction/previous-token attention-score rise earlier. Baseline models usually form one and sometimes two induction heads, whereas 4x models often form three. These are plot- and threshold-based observations without reported inferential statistics across the four seeds.

key_findings.claim: Suppressing the induction data direction changes the broader susceptibility geometry and predictive loss as well as the intended circuit, so the intervention is not fully surgical.
key_findings.evidence: For the first seed, PC2 explained variance is 0.98% under Repress-0x versus 2.24% in the original model and 2.96% in Baseline-1x; Induce-2x and Induce-4x give 2.88% and 2.16%. Appendix plots also show changes to Word Part, Word End, Numeric, and Left Delimiter susceptibilities. Repress-0x has the highest original-distribution loss, while Baseline-1x has the lowest; the paper reports curves rather than final numeric losses or uncertainty.

anchors.section: A.4 Susceptibilities PCA and Explained Variance

key_findings.claim: Manual data interventions provide two qualitative sanity checks: removing repeated-space runs disperses the spacing fin, while inserting long right-brace runs grows a new delimiter fin organized by run length.
key_findings.evidence: The spacing corpus replacement collapses consecutive spaces/newlines, and the delimiter corpus replaces a right brace with a uniformly random run of 1-50 braces with 50% probability. UMAPs of susceptibility vectors show the original spacing-fin organization lost and a new delimiter fin attached to the body. The delimiter model's original-distribution loss is visually close to the unmodified model; these checks use UMAP appearance and no quantitative structure metric.

key_findings.claim: On the parentheses task, whole-model susceptibility gaps identify interpretable in-distribution samples that distinguish models behaving like Nested from models behaving like Equal-Count out of distribution.
key_findings.evidence: The audit uses 30 pre-existing 2- or 3-layer, four-head Transformers with 0.001 weight decay. Susceptibilities are measured for 1,024 training examples; the mean of the three highest-OOD models (accuracies 0.915, 0.914, 0.911) and three lowest (0.111, 0.001, 0.000) approximates the two solution-specific rows. Large positive gaps produce 'almost nested' false sequences, while large negative gaps yield 'almost equal' false sequences. This extreme-model labeling assumes OOD behavior cleanly identifies the learned algorithm.

key_findings.claim: The LLC response verifies the intended direction for Almost Nested but falsifies the intended mechanism for Almost Equal.
key_findings.evidence: Across 15 original models, Almost Nested raises the local learning coefficient mainly for high-OOD/Nested solutions while leaving low-OOD/Equal-Count models nearly unchanged. Almost Equal was designed to raise Equal-Count LLC, but instead lowers LLC across the board and lowers it more for high-OOD/Nested models. The authors attribute this mismatch to a possible breakdown of the infinitesimal linear-response approximation under a finite distribution change.

key_findings.claim: Finite enrichment shifts the distribution of learned parentheses rules in opposite directions, with a much stronger effect for the rarer Almost Nested sample class.
key_findings.evidence: For each of the original, Almost Nested, and Almost Equal distributions, the authors train 100 models (10 initializations by 10 shuffles). Mean OOD accuracy is 0.310 on the original data, 0.004 on Almost Nested, and 0.497 on Almost Equal; all 100 Almost Nested runs are described as converging to Equal-Count. The modified 200,000-example corpora replace 36,600 false examples with two copies of 18,300 Almost Nested examples or 67,100 false examples with four copies of 19,000 Almost Equal examples. Random generation yields about 500 versus 3,700 qualifying examples per 100,000, supporting the rarity explanation but not isolating it experimentally.

key_findings.claim: The empirical interventions do not by themselves establish that pseudo-inversion or LLC-mediated Bayesian model selection is the unique cause of the behavioral shifts.
key_findings.evidence: The induction study applies thresholded weights derived from one PC rather than comparing the full pseudo-inverse with random-, frequency-, loss-, or gradient-matched reweightings. The parentheses study enriches hand-characterized sample classes, and the behavioral direction survives even when the Almost Equal LLC mechanism is opposite the prediction. The paper explicitly states that the SGD-posterior correspondence is a hypothesis, not a theorem.

key_findings.claim: Current susceptibility estimation is dramatically more expensive than the training run it is used to steer.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix estimates about 15 million sample-forward-pass equivalents to train the 3M model, 40 million for one checkpoint's susceptibility UMAP (about 3x training), and 7.7 billion to collect enough susceptibilities for the induction-patterning experiment (about 500x training). The authors propose auxiliary predictors, fewer weight restrictions, dynamic control, and critical-window intervention as untested scaling routes.

key_findings.claim: The alignment applications are proposals, not validated safety results.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix D extrapolates from induction and parentheses experiments to specification gaming, instrumental convergence, reward hacking, and constraints on undesirable structure. The authors explicitly state that scaling to frontier models and demonstrating the complete chain from susceptibility to safety outcomes remain open.

method.core_idea: Treat posterior structural observables as differentiable coordinates of the training distribution, estimate their Jacobian with susceptibility covariances, and invert that Jacobian to reweight examples toward a desired internal configuration or solution basin.
method.mechanism: A localized annealed posterior defines expectation values of component-loss observables or whole-model local-learning-coefficient observables. Per-example susceptibility is minus the posterior covariance of an observable with the example loss relative to population loss. Columns of these response vectors form chi; SVD identifies coupled data/structure modes, and chi's Moore-Penrose inverse gives the linear minimum-norm intervention. The language-model experiment projects 16 per-head susceptibilities onto induction-associated PC2 and maps scores below -2 through token weights 0x, 1x, 2x, or 4x. The parentheses experiment estimates solution-specific susceptibilities from extreme-OOD models, converts high-gap sequences into two synthetic training distributions, measures LLC shifts with localized SGLD, and retrains model populations to observe which OOD rule appears.
assumptions: Posterior expectation values of the selected observables vary smoothly enough with data-mixture coordinates that first-order response predicts the finite reweightings used in training.

The Euclidean coordinate norm in the chosen data-weight basis is the relevant notion of a minimum intervention, and the pseudo-inverse solution can be converted into feasible nonnegative sample weights.
Localized SGLD samples accurately estimate posterior covariances and LLCs with the selected inverse temperatures, localization strengths, step sizes, chains, and draws.
Attention-head susceptibility PC2 is a stable proxy for the induction-circuit-versus-rest-of-model mode across seeds and during the retraining trajectory.
The 4,000-step susceptibility subset, repeated for multiple epochs to about 20,000 steps, is representative enough that data reuse does not qualitatively change circuit development.
OOD accuracy on excluded equal-count-but-not-nested strings categorically identifies a Nested or Equal-Count internal algorithm, including intermediate-accuracy models.
The top and bottom three of 30 models provide adequate estimates of solution-local susceptibility rows for selecting synthetic samples.
Among equal-training-loss solutions, lower LLC drives greater Bayesian posterior weight, and SGD training frequencies track that posterior preference closely enough for intervention design.

Changes in LLC and behavior are attributable to the targeted sample geometry rather than duplication, false-class composition, sample frequency, optimization dynamics, or other unmeasured distribution statistics.
Component-local posterior observables are meaningfully connected to downstream generalization and, prospectively, to safety-relevant computations.

techniques.role: Expresses the derivative of a structural expectation with respect to an example or mixture perturbation as an annealed-posterior covariance.
Decomposes the response matrix into paired principal structures and principal data patterns with coupling strengths.
Maps a target structural-coordinate change back to a minimum-Euclidean-norm first-order data reweighting.
Samples localized tempered posteriors to estimate component susceptibilities and local learning coefficients without Hessian inversion.
Turns each token's induction-mode loading into a piecewise-linear 0x, 1x, 2x, or 4x loss weight during retraining.
Tracks induction formation through prefix-matching and previous-token scores across training checkpoints and seeds.
Ranks parentheses samples by the difference between susceptibility estimates from high- and low-OOD solution basins.
Operationalizes extreme susceptibility examples as reproducible Almost Nested and Almost Equal generators and substitutes them into a fixed-size corpus.
Uses 10 seeds by 10 dataset shuffles per condition to measure changes in the distribution of OOD rules rather than one selected model.
Checks non-target pattern susceptibilities, PCA geometry, and original-distribution loss for damage outside the intended structure.

evaluations.setting: 3M-parameter, two-layer, eight-head-per-layer attention-only Transformer; truncated 5,000-token GPT-2 vocabulary; repeated subset of filtered-Pile data; four seeds per token-weight condition; training to about 20,000 steps
evaluations.metric: Induction-pattern per-head susceptibility, prefix-matching score, previous-token score, and count of induction heads
evaluations.result: Repress-0x yields roughly one-tenth the induction susceptibility and almost no induction-score rise; 2x and 4x accelerate the rise; Baseline usually has one and sometimes two induction heads while 4x often has three
evaluations.baseline: Baseline-1x uses identical data and unit token weights; no random-, frequency-, loss-, or gradient-matched reweighting baseline is reported

evaluations.setting: First seed from the four induction-weighting conditions plus the original language model
evaluations.result: Original 2.24%, Baseline-1x 2.96%, Repress-0x 0.98%, Induce-2x 2.88%, and Induce-4x 2.16%
evaluations.baseline: Original and Baseline-1x geometries; only one seed per condition is tabulated

evaluations.setting: Induction weighting evaluated on the original distribution across all predefined token patterns
evaluations.metric: Per-pattern susceptibility curves and test-loss curves
evaluations.result: The target induction response changes most, but Word Part, Word End, Numeric, and Left Delimiter responses also move; Baseline-1x has the lowest test loss and Repress-0x the highest
evaluations.baseline: Baseline-1x; the paper reports plots without final losses or uncertainty

evaluations.setting: Manual repeated-spacing removal and repeated-right-brace insertion in the same small-language-model family
evaluations.metric: UMAP organization of per-token susceptibility vectors and test loss
evaluations.result: The spacing fin disperses, a new delimiter fin appears ordered by run length, and delimiter-fin loss is visually close to unmodified loss on original data
evaluations.baseline: Original model UMAP and loss; no quantitative fin-separation score or matched random edit

evaluations.setting: 30 parentheses models with 2 or 3 layers, four attention heads, weight decay 0.001; 1,024 uniformly sampled training examples
evaluations.metric: Whole-model per-sample susceptibility gap between averages of the three highest- and three lowest-OOD models
evaluations.result: Extreme gaps produce interpretable Almost Nested and Almost Equal false examples used to define synthetic generators
evaluations.baseline: Uniform training samples and the opposite solution-extreme group; selection uses only six of 30 models

evaluations.setting: 15 original parentheses models evaluated on original, Almost Nested, and Almost Equal corpora
evaluations.metric: Localized-SGLD estimate of whole-model local learning coefficient versus OOD test accuracy
evaluations.result: Almost Nested selectively increases LLC for high-OOD models; Almost Equal unexpectedly decreases LLC for all models and more strongly for high-OOD models
evaluations.baseline: LLC on the original distribution; the Almost Equal direction is an explicit failed prediction

evaluations.setting: Three 200,000-example parentheses distributions; 100 fresh models per distribution from 10 initializations by 10 shuffles; five epochs
evaluations.metric: OOD accuracy on equal-count but incorrectly nested sequences
evaluations.result: Mean OOD accuracy changes from 0.310 original to 0.004 Almost Nested and 0.497 Almost Equal; all 100 Almost Nested runs are characterized as Equal-Count
evaluations.baseline: Original distribution is bimodal; no equally sized random-false-example replacement or non-susceptibility hard-example baseline

evaluations.metric: Qualifying samples per 100,000 uniformly generated parentheses strings
evaluations.result: Approximately 500 meet Almost Nested criteria versus 3,700 meeting Almost Equal criteria
evaluations.baseline: Relative natural prevalence supports but does not experimentally identify the cause of the asymmetric retraining effect

evaluations.setting: Compute accounting for the 3M language-model experiments
evaluations.result: Training about 15 million; one checkpoint UMAP about 40 million (approximately 3x); induction-patterning susceptibility collection about 7.7 billion (approximately 500x)
evaluations.baseline: One ordinary training run; projected larger-model scaling is analytical rather than measured here

limitations: Author-stated: experiments use a 3M-parameter language model and a simple synthetic classification task; the study does not establish scaling to larger or frontier models.
Author-stated: susceptibility estimation is computationally expensive; the induction intervention consumes an estimated 500 times the sample-forward passes of training the small model.
Author-stated: only one-off interventions fixed before training are tested; online control that updates weights as structure develops remains future work.
Author-stated: the theory is infinitesimal but the interventions are finite, and the Almost Equal LLC result demonstrates that the predicted local direction can break down.
Author-stated: the mapping from structural observables to downstream safety properties has not been established.
Author-stated: identifying posterior preference with SGD outcomes is a supported hypothesis rather than a theorem.
Reviewer-identified: the induction study has four seeds per condition and the PCA table only one; no confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, or seed-level effect sizes are reported.
Reviewer-identified: the thresholded PC2 masks do not implement or compare the full pseudo-inverse solution, so the central optimization claim receives only a single-mode demonstration.

Reviewer-identified: susceptibility collection covers enough unique data for about 4,000 steps and repeats it for multiple epochs, introducing a data-reuse confound relative to ordinary 50,000-step training.
Reviewer-identified: UMAP fins are qualitative and can depend on embedding hyperparameters; no quantitative cluster/shape statistic is reported.
Reviewer-identified: the parentheses corpus duplicates selected false examples while removing other false examples, with no random replacement, hardness-matched, or conventional curriculum baseline.

Reviewer-identified: high or low OOD accuracy is treated as an algorithm label even though attention ablations in the source task show that predictive internal patterns need not be causal implementations.
Reviewer-identified: the minimum-norm solution depends on the coordinate system and ignores finite-data simplex constraints, nonnegative weights, and modes outside the probed example/component basis.
Reviewer-identified: the paper offers no held-out susceptibility-estimation replication, no direct comparison with influence/gradient methods, and no prospective safety evaluation.
failure_modes: A target component outside chi's column space cannot be reached by the available data perturbations; small singular values also make the pseudo-inverse amplify estimator noise.

Finite weights can leave the local linear regime, reverse the predicted observable response, or violate nonnegative-probability constraints; Almost Equal is the in-paper example of a mechanism reversal.
SGLD non-convergence, poor localization, or multimodal posterior geometry can corrupt both susceptibilities and LLC comparisons.
A PC direction can encode an opposition between the target circuit and the rest of the model rather than the target alone, producing collateral changes despite nominally mode-aligned weighting.
Repeated training on a small susceptibility-scored subset can teach duplication artifacts or change memorization dynamics rather than selectively shaping the intended circuit.
Suppressing common induction tokens impairs original-distribution loss, so absence of a circuit may reflect removed predictive signal rather than precise structural control at fixed capability.
Synthetic sample enrichment can select a rule through ordinary feature frequency or optimization bias even when the hypothesized LLC direction is wrong.
OOD-accuracy categories can conceal hybrid algorithms or different mechanisms with the same behavior, making solution-local susceptibility rows mis-specified.
The susceptibility map changes during training; a fixed pre-training intervention can become stale or push later stages in an unintended direction.
Scaling may be blocked by the number of components, data examples, SGLD draws, and checkpoints even if per-restriction compute grows more slowly than optimal-training compute.
Safety-relevant computations may be distributed, context-dependent, or adversarially hidden, so a selected observable may not faithfully represent the property to suppress.
reusable_insights: Write data intervention as an explicit Jacobian inverse problem and report the null space and singular spectrum before claiming a target is controllable.
Separate the predicted direction of an internal observable from the final behavioral direction; an intervention can work behaviorally while falsifying its proposed mechanism.
Use solution-specific complexity responses when multiple rules fit the same training data, but validate them on held-out models rather than only extreme prototypes.
Audit collateral structure and ordinary loss alongside the target circuit; a successful control should not be inferred from one mechanism score alone.
Population retraining over both initialization and data order is more informative than a single selected seed when the outcome is which algorithm emerges.
Record sample-generation criteria and replacement counts exactly so a targeted curriculum can be compared with random, frequency-matched, and hardness-matched alternatives.
Treat one-off reweighting as a local controller whose validity must be rechecked after the model moves; online recalibration is the natural next experiment.
Include a compute ratio against training, because a structurally principled data selector can be practically dominated by much cheaper gradient or representation heuristics.
Use explicit negative predictions, such as the Almost Equal LLC direction, to bound what the linear-response theory currently explains.
open_questions: Does the full constrained pseudo-inverse outperform thresholded PC weighting, gradient similarity, influence functions, loss-based curricula, and random/frequency-matched reweighting at equal compute?
Over what perturbation radius does measured susceptibility accurately predict LLC or circuit changes, and can curvature terms forecast the Almost Equal reversal?
Can online susceptibility updates achieve the same structural control with less data distortion and compute than a one-off 0x-4x mask?
Do induction-control effects replicate in larger models, richer tokenizers, MLP-containing architectures, full 50,000-step data streams, and natural held-out language behavior?
Which model checkpoints are critical control windows, and can susceptibility estimation be restricted to those windows without losing effect?
Are OOD-rule shifts mediated by LLC after controlling sample rarity, duplication, margin, gradient norm, and conventional example hardness?
Can hybrid or mechanistically distinct parentheses solutions be separated with causal interventions rather than OOD accuracy alone?
How stable are susceptibility modes across seeds, component bases, localization choices, SGLD diagnostics, and alternative priors?
Can auxiliary susceptibility predictors preserve sign and rank on held-out samples and architectures well enough to close the 500x compute gap?
What observable and prospective benchmark would demonstrate that patterning changes a safety property without degrading useful capability or merely changing surface behavior?

competitive_landscape.title: Structural Inference: Interpreting Small Language Models with Susceptibilities
competitive_landscape.difference: Baker et al. define the posterior linear-response susceptibility, its per-token attribution, and the low-rank component/data response matrix in the same 3M Transformer. Patterning's new step is to pseudo-invert that already-measured map and retrain on the resulting direction; it therefore extends rather than originates susceptibility-based structural inference.

competitive_landscape.title: Embryology of a Language Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. follow the same susceptibility geometry through training, identify induction-linked PC2 and the spacing fin, and use UMAP to describe emerging organization. The target turns those descriptive developmental signatures into fixed corpus interventions and adds an algorithm-selection study.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Interpretation Predict Behavior on Unseen Data?
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. introduce the parentheses distribution and train hundreds of Transformers whose in-distribution attention predicts Nested versus Equal-Count OOD behavior, while causal ablations show that predictive patterns need not implement the rule. Patterning reuses that task and model population but intervenes on susceptibility-selected in-distribution samples to shift the population of OOD outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Spectroscopy: Susceptibility Clusters in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Gordon et al. theoretically decompose susceptibility by data modes and cluster Pythia-14M token responses into 510 interpretable groups, with 50% matching SAE features. It remains a read/cluster method; the target uses mode inversion and retraining to attempt to write a chosen structure.

competitive_landscape.title: Bayesian Influence Functions for Hessian-Free Data Attribution
competitive_landscape.difference: Kreer et al. use local posterior statistics and stochastic-gradient MCMC to build Hessian-free Bayesian influence functions that predict retraining effects at billion-parameter scale. Their target is prediction/data attribution, whereas Patterning targets component or LLC observables and designs a reweighting; a compute- and retraining-matched comparison is absent.

competitive_landscape.title: LESS: Selecting Influential Data for Targeted Instruction Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: LESS performs optimizer-aware low-rank gradient-similarity selection from a reusable datastore and reports that 5% selected instruction data can beat the full set on target skills, including transfer from smaller to larger models. Patterning instead uses expensive posterior covariances to target internal structure rather than downstream validation behavior and does not benchmark against LESS-like gradients.

competitive_landscape.title: TRAK: Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
competitive_landscape.difference: TRAK approximates training-data influence with random-projected after-kernel features from a handful of trained models across image, vision-language, and language settings. It attributes prediction-level behavior efficiently; Patterning targets posterior internal observables and uses the inverse response for control, but its small-model evidence costs roughly 500 training runs in forward-pass equivalents.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim Patterning is the dual of mechanistic interpretability: the same susceptibility mathematics used to read internal structure can be inverted to write it through training-data interventions, including both circuit modulation and selection between equally training-compatible algorithms.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies the pseudo-inverse/SVD formulation, four-condition induction retraining, two qualitative fin interventions, solution-local LLC measurements, and 300 fresh parentheses retrainings. It demonstrates strong directional effects on induction scores and OOD-rule frequencies, preserves a failed LLC-direction prediction, and reports collateral structure, loss, and compute costs.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the explicit Jacobian-pseudo-inverse framing plus demonstrations that susceptibility-derived data directions can alter a known circuit and the population frequency of OOD rules. Susceptibilities, induction PC2, the spacing fin, the parentheses task, influence-based retraining prediction, and targeted data selection all predate it. Because the main circuit mask is a thresholded single-PC heuristic, the Almost Equal mechanism reverses, Bayesian-SGD correspondence is assumed, and matched data-selection baselines are absent, the evidence supports an initial small-scale proof of susceptibility-guided structural steering, not a general solution to prescribing training data for arbitrary generalization or safety properties.

reviewer_notes: Verified against all 30 pages of arXiv v1, including every appendix section, equation, table-equivalent numeric list, figure caption, SGLD setting, synthetic-data recipe, compute estimate, and alignment qualification. PDF render checks covered the induction curves, LLC/OOD histograms, PC2 values, and loss plots; no quantitative value above was inferred from plot pixels. The negative/contradiction audit retained collateral pattern changes, higher Repress loss, the failed Almost Equal LLC mechanism, finite-versus-infinitesimal mismatch, SGD-posterior caveat, qualitative UMAP evidence, sample reuse, and the absence of matched selection baselines. Seven current primary records were opened and version-pinned on 2026-08-23. Confidence remains below 0.9 because several central claims are graphical, four-seed or one-seed analyses, the behavioral mechanism is not isolated, and scaling/safety claims are prospective.

verification.passage_check: Second pass checked each finding against its cited PDF pages after an end-to-end reading of pages 1-30, including Sections 1-6, Appendices A-D, all equations, figures, numeric settings, negative results, and author qualifications; PDF and text hashes plus page count were matched exactly to fulltext_index.jsonl.
verification.competitor_check: Second pass opened all seven canonical arXiv records, verified exact titles, current revisions and abstracts/full records as of 2026-08-23, and compared mechanisms, tasks, compute, and evidence rather than title similarity; arxiv:2601.13548 itself was excluded.
